sourceText: The LEGUIN-ANARRES sector was already in progress when they entered. For several lessons Aster had refused to pause worlds for their arrival; the fact that a class was visiting was not a cosmic event for the inhabitants. A society without formal property nevertheless retains conformity, reputation, and dependence on communal cooperation. The memorial bore the name of Ursula K. Le Guin — The Dispossessed precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The children discovered that technology often solves the problem it can measure and moves the conflict into a variable it never measured. Marae kept her local body vulnerable. Pain, fatigue, and the impossibility of doing ten things at once were epistemic instruments for her, not biological scenery. At the center of the conflict was Noma, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 223 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: Kesh discovers that institutions do not disappear when their names disappear. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Ap — Planetary Anarchism: institutions operate without a coercive central state; At — Attention Economy: attention becomes the scarce resource. Course references included Le Guin — The Dispossessed; network fiction. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Kesh broke the first consensus. ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ Vela answered without raising their voice: ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became 224 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Vela evaluated the solution not by efficiency but by the differences it made invisible. She found one: a local minority for whom the proposed “improvement” destroyed a practice with no equivalent. Optimizing the average concealed a small and perfectly legal extinction. The night did not end in victory. Orin writes that the problem is not abolishing power but making it visible and contestable. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. Tern no longer called the anomaly a “signal.” He used the more modest term residue. He found it only after excluding the explanations he wanted to be true. Vela helped precisely through skepticism: if a hypothesis survived a sister motivated to destroy it, it deserved another night. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the REFLEXIVITY operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — makes description, prediction, belief, or observation modify the thing described — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 225 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 226 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
